question.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(1)y(1)+x(0)y(0)+x(-1)y(-1).
$$

If $p(t)=k{t}^{2}-2t$ and $q(t)=2t+1$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
question.worked_solution:
Since $p(t)$ and $q(t)$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =p(1)q(1)+p(0)q(0)+p(-1)q(-1) \\  & =(k-2)(2+1)+(0)(0+1)+(k+2)(-2+1) \\  & =(3k-6)+0+(-k-2) \\  & =2k-8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =0 \\ 2k-8 & =0 \\ 2k & =8 \\ k & =4\end{aligned}
$$
